source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice short questions written from Chapter 6 (PDF 117-143), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh chapter 6 (Chemical Energetics) ke poore chapter se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, chapter ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal ka mukhtasar model jawab hai; chhote numericals mein hal ke qadam hain, aur farq wale sawal ka jawab table mein hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 What is thermochemistry? Why is it also called energetics?
(Thermochemistry kya hai? Ise energetics kyun kehte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Thermochemistry physical ya chemical tabdeeliyon mein jazb ya kharij heat energy ki miqdaar ka mutaala hai. Kyun ke yeh energy ki tabdeeliyon se mutaliq hai is liye ise energetics bhi kehte hain; yeh zyada tar first law of thermodynamics par mabni hai.

book_ref.quote: That is why it is also called energetics

blocks.prompt:
2 What does thermodynamics allow us to predict about a reaction?
(Thermodynamics hamein reaction ke baare mein kya pehle se batane deti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Thermodynamics batati hai ke koi khaas reaction di gayi conditions mein ho sakta hai ya nahi, yani yeh reaction ki spontaneity (khud ba khud hone) par baat karti hai.

book_ref.quote: Moreover, thermodynamics allows us to predict whether a particular reaction can occur under specified conditions

blocks.prompt:
3 What is meant by enthalpy change? Write its mathematical form.
(Enthalpy change se kya muraad hai? Is ki riyazi shakal likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Enthalpy change (ΔH) woh khalis energy hai jo reactants ke products banne par heat ki shakal mein kharij ya jazb hoti hai, kyun ke products ki kul enthalpy (HP) reactants (HR) ke barabar nahi hoti.
ΔH = HP – HR

book_ref.quote: enthalpy change is the net energy, which is either evolved or absorbed in the form of heat

blocks.prompt:
4 Why is the total enthalpy of the products never equal to that of the reactants?
(Products ki kul enthalpy reactants ke barabar kyun nahi hoti?)
blocks.explanation: Har substance ki apni makhsoos enthalpy hoti hai jo us ki structure (bonds ki qisam) aur physical state par depend karti hai. Products aur reactants mukhtalif substances hain, is liye HP ≠ HR aur har reaction mein ΔH hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Every substance possesses a characteristic amount of enthalpy.

blocks.prompt:
5 Give one example each of an exothermic and an endothermic process, with ΔH values.
(Exothermic aur endothermic process ki aik aik misaal ΔH ke saath dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Exothermic: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = –393.7 kJ mol⁻¹.
Endothermic: NH₄Cl(s) + H₂O(l) → NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), ΔH = +16.2 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The dissolution of ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) in water is an endothermic process.

blocks.prompt:
6 How does a cold pack work?
(Cold pack kaise kaam karta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Cold pack mein paani aur NH₄Cl ke crystals hote hain. Pack dabane par yeh mil jate hain; NH₄Cl ka hal hona endothermic hai, is liye surroundings se energy jazb hoti hai aur thandak mehsoos hoti hai. Yeh andaruni chot ke ilaaj mein istemal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: When the pack is kneaded, water and NH₄Cl crystals mix and energy is absorbed from the surroundings

blocks.prompt:
7 For a reaction HR = 180 kJ and HP = 245 kJ. Find ΔH and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
(Aik reaction mein HR = 180 kJ aur HP = 245 kJ hai. ΔH nikalein aur batayein ke reaction exothermic hai ya endothermic.)
blocks.explanation: ΔH = HP – HR = 245 – 180 = +65 kJ. ΔH positive hai (HP > HR), is liye heat jazb hoti hai: reaction endothermic hai.

book_ref.quote: ii. HP > HR: such reactions involve an increase in enthalpy

blocks.prompt:
8 Define energy of activation.
(Energy of activation ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Energy of activation (Ea) woh kam az kam energy hai jo reactant molecules ko energy barrier paar karne ke liye chahiye. Bond todne ke liye molecules ka kam az kam itni energy se takrana zaroori hai.

book_ref.quote: This minimum amount of energy required by the reactant molecules just to cross that energy barrier is called energy of activation

blocks.prompt:
9 What does an energy profile diagram show for an exothermic and an endothermic reaction?
(Energy profile diagram exothermic aur endothermic reaction ke liye kya dikhata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh reactants aur products ki energy aur un ke darmiyan energy barrier (Ea) dikhata hai. Exothermic mein products reactants se neeche (ΔH negative) aur endothermic mein products reactants se oopar (ΔH positive) hote hain.

book_ref.quote: The energy profile diagram of exothermic and endothermic reactions are given in Figure 6.2.

blocks.prompt:
10 What are standard conditions for enthalpy changes? Why are they needed?
(Enthalpy changes ki standard conditions kya hain? Inki zaroorat kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Standard conditions: temperature 25 °C (298 K) aur pressure 1 atm (101 kPa). Inki zaroorat is liye hai ke enthalpy physical state, pressure aur temperature par depend karti hai, is liye durust muqable ke liye conditions muqarrar honi chahiye.

book_ref.quote: Hence, we must specify these conditions while writing an equation.

blocks.prompt:
11 What is the standard state of an element? What is ΔH°f of an element in its standard state?
(Element ki standard state kya hai? Standard state mein element ka ΔH°f kitna hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Element ki standard state 298 K aur 1 atm par us ki sab se mustahkam shakal hai, maslan carbon ke liye graphite (diamond nahi). Definition ke mutabiq standard state mein har element ka ΔH°f zero hota hai.

book_ref.quote: The standard state of an element is its most stable form at 298 K and 1atm pressure.

blocks.prompt:
12 Define standard enthalpy of reaction with an example.
(Standard enthalpy of reaction ki definition misaal ke saath likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh woh enthalpy change hai jab stoichiometric miqdaar mein reactants apni standard states mein standard conditions par poori tarah react kar ke products banayein.
Misaal: H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l), ΔHr = –286 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: consider the reaction between hydrogen and oxygen gases to form 1 mole of water

blocks.prompt:
13 Define standard enthalpy change of combustion. Write the equation for ethanol.
(Standard enthalpy change of combustion ki definition likhein. Ethanol ki equation likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh woh enthalpy change hai jab aik mole substance standard conditions par zyada oxygen mein poori tarah jale. Yeh hamesha exothermic hoti hai.
C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The standard enthalpy change of combustion of a substance is the enthalpy change involved

blocks.prompt:
14 How much heat is evolved when 0.40 mol of ethanol is burnt completely (ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹)?
(0.40 mol ethanol poori tarah jalne par kitni heat kharij hogi (ΔH°c = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹)?)
blocks.explanation: Kharij heat = 0.40 mol × 1368 kJ mol⁻¹ = 547.2 kJ (ΔH = –547.2 kJ).

book_ref.quote: standard enthalpy of combustion ΔH°C of ethanol is –1368 kJ mol⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
15 Define standard enthalpy change of formation. Give the equation for methane.
(Standard enthalpy change of formation ki definition likhein. Methane ki equation dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh woh enthalpy change hai jab standard conditions par aik mole compound apne elements se bane. Yeh exothermic ya endothermic ho sakti hai.
C(s) + 2H₂(g) → CH₄(g), ΔH°f = –74.8 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: Standard enthalpy change of formation of a compound is the enthalpy change involved

blocks.prompt:
16 Define standard enthalpy change of atomization. Why is ΔH°at of hydrogen half of the H–H bond energy?
(Standard enthalpy change of atomization ki definition likhein. Hydrogen ka ΔH°at H–H bond energy ka aadha kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh woh enthalpy change hai jab standard conditions par element se aik mole gaseous atoms banein. Aik mole H–H bond todne (H₂ → 2H, +436 kJ mol⁻¹) se do mole atoms bante hain, is liye aik mole ke liye: ½H₂(g) → H(g), ΔH°at = +218 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The standard enthalpy change of atomization of an element is the enthalpy change involved when one mole of gaseous atoms

blocks.prompt:
17 Define standard enthalpy change of neutralization. Write the actual neutralization reaction.
(Standard enthalpy change of neutralization ki definition likhein. Asal neutralization reaction likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh woh enthalpy change hai jab standard conditions par acid aur alkali ke reaction se aik mole paani bane. Yeh hamesha exothermic hai.
H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l), ΔH°n = –57.1 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The standard enthalpy change of neutralization is the enthalpy change involved

blocks.prompt:
18 Why is ΔH°n for all strong acid–strong base reactions nearly the same (about –57.1 kJ mol⁻¹)?
(Tamam strong acid–strong base reactions ka ΔH°n taqreeban aik jaisa (–57.1 kJ mol⁻¹) kyun hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Strong acids aur bases poori tarah ionize hote hain. Milane par sirf H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) hota hai; baqi ions (maslan Na⁺, Cl⁻) aazad rehte hain. Is liye ΔH°n sirf ions se aik mole paani banne ki heat hai jo har dafa aik jaisi hai.

book_ref.quote: Thus, the enthalpy of neutralization is merely the heat of formation of one mole of liquid water from its ionic components

blocks.prompt:
19 Define first electron affinity. Why does it carry a negative sign for chlorine?
(First electron affinity ki definition likhein. Chlorine ke liye yeh negative kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: First electron affinity woh enthalpy change hai jab standard conditions par 1 mole gaseous atoms mein 1 mole electrons add ho kar 1 mole gaseous uni-negative ions banein. Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻, ΔH = –348.8 kJ mol⁻¹; energy kharij hoti hai is liye sign negative hai.

book_ref.quote: The first electron affinity is the enthalpy change involved when 1 mole of electrons is added

blocks.prompt:
20 Distinguish between standard enthalpy of combustion and standard enthalpy of atomization.
(Standard enthalpy of combustion aur standard enthalpy of atomization mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Combustion mein aik mole substance oxygen mein jalta hai; atomization mein element se aik mole gaseous atoms bante hain.

book_ref.quote: For instance, ΔH°f for methane is given below.

rows: Aik mole substance zyada oxygen mein poori tarah jalta hai.
Element se aik mole gaseous atoms bante hain.
Hamesha exothermic (negative).
Energy jazb hoti hai (positive), maslan H ke liye +218 kJ mol⁻¹.
Misaal: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l), –1368 kJ mol⁻¹.
Misaal: ½H₂(g) → H(g), +218 kJ mol⁻¹.

blocks.text: 6.4 Bond energy (bond dissociation energy) and enthalpy changes

blocks.prompt:
21 Define bond dissociation energy.
(Bond dissociation energy ki definition likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Bond dissociation energy (E) woh average energy hai jo kisi substance mein khaas bond ke aik mole ko todne ke liye chahiye. Utni hi energy bond banne par kharij hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: The same amount of energy is absorbed when the bond is broken to form neutral atoms

blocks.prompt:
22 Differentiate between exact bond energy and average bond energy.
(Exact bond energy aur average bond energy mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Exact bond energy aik khaas substance ke bond ki hai; average bond energy mukhtalif molecules ki average hai.

book_ref.quote: When we take average of all Ec-c in different molecules, we obtain average C-C bond energy.

rows: Kisi khaas substance mein khaas bond ki energy.
Mukhtalif molecules mein us bond ki energies ki average.
Misaal: ethane mein EC–C = 376 kJ mol⁻¹.
Misaal: average EC–C = 348 kJ mol⁻¹ (Table 6.1).
Har compound mein mukhtalif.
Amli hisaab mein istemal hoti hai.

blocks.prompt:
23 Why do C–C bonds have different bond energies in ethane, propane and butane?
(Ethane, propane aur butane mein C–C bonds ki bond energies mukhtalif kyun hain?)
blocks.explanation: Bond energy molecule ke doosre atoms se mutasir hoti hai. Is liye C–C bond ethane mein 376, propane mein 356 aur butane mein 352 kJ mol⁻¹ hai; aam tor par C–C ki qeemat 350 se 380 kJ mol⁻¹ hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Actually, B.E. is affected by other atoms in a molecule.

blocks.text: 6.5 Enthalpy change of reaction and chemical bonds

blocks.prompt:
24 Where does the enthalpy change of a reaction come from?
(Reaction ka enthalpy change kahan se aata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Chemical reaction mein purane bonds tootte aur naye bante hain. Bond todna energy jazb karta hai (+ve) aur bond banana energy kharij karta hai (–ve); in ka farq ΔHr hai.

book_ref.quote: Therefore, the enthalpy change (ΔHr) in a chemical reaction actually comes from the breaking and forming of chemical bonds.

blocks.prompt:
25 When is a reaction exothermic and when is it endothermic in terms of bond energies?
(Bond energies ke lihaaz se reaction kab exothermic aur kab endothermic hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Exothermic: naye bonds banne mein kharij energy, bonds todne mein jazb energy se zyada ho. Endothermic: bonds todne mein jazb energy, naye bonds banne mein kharij energy se zyada ho.

book_ref.quote: The reverse is true for an endothermic reaction.

blocks.prompt:
26 Using bond energies EH–H = 436, EO=O = 498 and EO–H = 463 kJ mol⁻¹, show that the formation of 2 mol of water vapour from H₂ and O₂ is exothermic.
(EH–H = 436, EO=O = 498 aur EO–H = 463 kJ mol⁻¹ le kar dikhayein ke H₂ aur O₂ se 2 mol paani ki bhaap banna exothermic hai.)
blocks.explanation:
2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g)
Toote bonds: 2(436) + 498 = 1370 kJ; bane bonds: 4(463) = 1852 kJ.
ΔH = 1370 – 1852 = –482 kJ; jazb se zyada energy kharij hui, is liye exothermic.

book_ref.quote: A chemical bond represents a form of energy known as chemical energy

blocks.text: 6.6 Measurement of the enthalpy change of a reaction

blocks.prompt:
27 Define specific heat capacity. What is its value for water?
(Specific heat capacity ki definition likhein. Paani ke liye is ki qeemat kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) woh heat energy hai jo kisi substance ki unit mass ka temperature 1 K (ya 1 °C) barhane ke liye chahiye. Paani ke liye c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ (fi gram), yani 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a substance

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book correction yaad rakhein: 4.18 J ki qeemat 1 g paani ke liye hai. 1 kg ke liye yeh 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ ban jati hai.

blocks.prompt:
28 Calculate the heat absorbed by 150 g of water when its temperature rises from 22.0 °C to 30.0 °C (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹).
(150 g paani ka temperature 22.0 °C se 30.0 °C tak barhe to kitni heat jazb hogi (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹)?)

book_ref.quote: Calorimetry relies on the fact that it takes 4.18J of energy

blocks.prompt:
29 For which reactions is a glass calorimeter suitable and for which is it not?
(Glass calorimeter kin reactions ke liye munasib hai aur kin ke liye nahi?)
blocks.explanation: Munasib: solutions mein reactions ki heat naapne ke liye (maslan neutralization). Ghair munasib: gases wale reactions (gas bahar nikal jayegi) aur woh reactions jin ke products bohat garam ho jate hain.

book_ref.quote: A glass calorimeter is suitable for measuring heat-flow for reactions in solutions.

blocks.prompt:
30 Name the parts of a glass calorimeter and give the purpose of its lid and cotton wool.
(Glass calorimeter ke hisson ke naam likhein aur dhakkan aur cotton wool ka maqsad batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Hisse: beaker, stirrer, thermometer aur dheela dhakkan. Dheela dhakkan contents ko atmospheric (constant) pressure par rakhta hai, is liye naapi gayi heat ΔH hoti hai. Cotton wool bahar ki deewaron ko insulate kar ke hawa se heat ka len-den kam karti hai.

book_ref.quote: It consists of a beaker, a stirrer, a thermometer and a loose-fitting lid

blocks.prompt:
31 50 cm³ of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ HCl is neutralized by 50 cm³ of 2.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH and the temperature rises by 13.6 °C. Find ΔH°n (mass of solution 100 g, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).
(50 cm³ 2.0 mol dm⁻³ HCl ko 50 cm³ 2.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH se neutralize kiya, temperature 13.6 °C barha. ΔH°n nikalein (solution ki mass 100 g, c = 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹).)

book_ref.quote: As all the heat evolved during the reaction remains within the calorimeter and absorbed by water, so

blocks.prompt:
32 Why can the volume of a dilute aqueous solution in cm³ be taken as its mass in grams in calorimeter calculations?
(Calorimeter ke hisaab mein dilute aqueous solution ka volume (cm³) uski mass (g) kyun maan liya jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: Solutions itne patle hain ke un ki mass taqreeban sab paani hai, aur paani ki density taqreeban 1 g cm⁻³ hai. Is liye maslan 200 cm³ solution ≈ 200 g, aur paani ki specific heat istemal ho sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: Density of H₂O is around 1gcm⁻³, so total volume of solution which is 200 cm³ ≈ 200 g

blocks.text: 6.7 Enthalpy change and calorie content of food

blocks.prompt:
33 What is meant by calorie content of food? In which units is it expressed?
(Khurak ke calorie content se kya muraad hai? Yeh kin units mein hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khurak ka calorie content us energy ka paimana hai jo khurak jism mein poori tarah istemal hone par kharij hoti hai. Yeh aam tor par kilocalories (kcal) ya joules (J) mein hota hai.

book_ref.quote: The calorie content of food is a measure of the energy ‘released’ when the food is completely consumed in the body.

blocks.prompt:
34 Why can the calorie content of a food be found by burning it in a calorimeter?
(Khurak ka calorie content calorimeter mein jala kar kyun maloom kiya ja sakta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khurak hazm hone par us ki chemical energy heat ki shakal mein kharij hoti hai. Hazm hone mein utni hi energy kharij hoti hai jitni bahar jalne par, is liye (bomb) calorimeter mein naapi gayi heat of combustion calorie content deti hai.

book_ref.quote: So, the overall enthalpy of combustion is the same as the heat of combustion

blocks.prompt:
35 Glucose burns with ΔH° = –2803 kJ mol⁻¹ (molar mass 180 g mol⁻¹). How much energy is obtained from 27 g of glucose?
(Glucose ΔH° = –2803 kJ mol⁻¹ ke saath jalta hai (molar mass 180 g mol⁻¹). 27 g glucose se kitni energy milegi?)

book_ref.quote: mol (180.0 g) of glucose burns to produce energy = 2803 kJ

blocks.prompt:
36 Why must the calorie content we take from food be balanced?
(Khurak se li gayi calories ka tawazun kyun zaroori hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khurak se li gayi calories ko kaam, warzish aur musbat sargarmiyon se barabar karna zaroori hai; warna jism ki nashonuma aur dekh bhaal be-tawazun ho jati hai.

book_ref.quote: Remember, the calorie content we take from food must be balanced by working, exercising

blocks.prompt:
37 State the law of conservation of energy. How is it related to Hess's law?
(Law of conservation of energy bayan karein. Is ka Hess's law se kya taaluq hai?)
blocks.explanation: Energy na paida ki ja sakti hai na khatam, sirf aik shakal se doosri mein badalti hai. First law of thermodynamics isi qanoon ka izhaar hai, aur Hess ne ise enthalpy changes par lagaya; Hess's law first law ka khaas case hai.

book_ref.quote: First law of thermodynamics is actually a manifestation of law of conservation of energy

blocks.prompt:
38 Why is Hess's law needed to find some enthalpy changes? Give one example.
(Kuch enthalpy changes ke liye Hess's law ki zaroorat kyun hai? Aik misaal dein.)
blocks.explanation: Bohat se reactions ka ΔH calorimetric tareeqe se seedha nahi naapa ja sakta. Misaal: CCl₄ carbon aur chlorine ko seedha mila kar nahi banta, is liye is ka ΔH°f Hess's law se nikala jata hai.

book_ref.quote: Germain Henri Hess applied the law of conservation of energy to enthalpy changes.

blocks.prompt:
39 What is a Hess cycle? What are reaction intermediates?
(Hess cycle kya hai? Reaction intermediates kya hain?)
blocks.explanation: Hess cycle (energy cycle) dikhata hai ke reactant A seedhe raaste se aur do ya zyada qadmon wale indirect raaston se product B banta hai; har raaste se ΔH aik jaisa hai (maslan ΔHr = ΔH₁ + ΔH₂). Indirect raaston ke qadmon mein banne wale products reaction intermediates kehlate hain.

book_ref.quote: Hess’s law can be illustrated by drawing enthalpy cycles, often called energy cycles or Hess cycles.

blocks.prompt:
40 Given ΔH°c(C, graphite) = –393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH°f(CO) = –110.5 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate ΔH°c of CO.
(ΔH°c(C, graphite) = –393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ aur ΔH°f(CO) = –110.5 kJ mol⁻¹ diye gaye hain. CO ka ΔH°c nikalein.)
blocks.explanation:
Seedha: C + O₂ → CO₂, ΔH = –393.5. Indirect: C + ½O₂ → CO (–110.5), phir CO + ½O₂ → CO₂ (ΔH₂).
–393.5 = –110.5 + ΔH₂ → ΔH₂ = –283 kJ mol⁻¹

book_ref.quote: Solution: Applying Hess’ law, we can write

blocks.prompt:
41 Write the expression for ΔH°r in terms of enthalpies of formation, and use it for C₂H₄(g) + HBr(g) → C₂H₅Br(g), given ΔH°f: C₂H₄ +52.2, HBr –36.3, C₂H₅Br –64.0 kJ mol⁻¹.
(ΔH°r ko enthalpies of formation ki shakal mein likhein, aur C₂H₄(g) + HBr(g) → C₂H₅Br(g) par lagayein; ΔH°f: C₂H₄ +52.2, HBr –36.3, C₂H₅Br –64.0 kJ mol⁻¹.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔH°r = ΣΔH°f(products) – ΣΔH°f(reactants)
= –64.0 – [52.2 + (–36.3)] = –64.0 – 15.9 = –79.9 kJ mol⁻¹

book_ref.quote: ΔH°f of C₂H₅Cl = -109 KJ mol⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
42 Write the version of Hess's law used with bond energies and explain its two steps.
(Bond energies ke saath istemal hone wala Hess's law likhein aur is ke do qadam samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔH°rxn = ΣnER – ΣnEP
Qadam 1: reactant molecules ke tamam bonds toot kar aazad gaseous atoms bante hain (bond energies ka jama, positive). Qadam 2: in atoms se product molecules bante hain (bond energies minus sign ke saath).

book_ref.quote: In general, the heat of reaction for any gaseous chemical reaction can be calculated from average B.E.’s

blocks.prompt:
43 Using Table 6.1 (EC–H = 413, ECl–Cl = 243, EC–Cl = 328, EH–Cl = 432 kJ mol⁻¹), estimate ΔH for CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₃Cl(g) + HCl(g).
(Table 6.1 (EC–H = 413, ECl–Cl = 243, EC–Cl = 328, EH–Cl = 432 kJ mol⁻¹) se CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₃Cl(g) + HCl(g) ka ΔH andaza karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Toote bonds: aik C–H + aik Cl–Cl = 413 + 243 = 656 kJ
Bane bonds: aik C–Cl + aik H–Cl = 328 + 432 = 760 kJ
ΔH = 656 – 760 = –104 kJ

book_ref.quote: use B.E. data from Table 6.1 to estimate ΔH for the reaction

blocks.prompt:
44 When 2.30 g of ethanol (46.0 g mol⁻¹) is burnt, 68.4 kJ of heat is evolved. Find the molar enthalpy of combustion of ethanol.
(Jab 2.30 g ethanol (46.0 g mol⁻¹) jalaya gaya to 68.4 kJ heat kharij hui. Ethanol ki molar enthalpy of combustion nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: When 14.64 g of propane is burned in an excess of oxygen in a calorimeter

blocks.prompt:
45 What is dissolution? Name the three steps assumed in the formation of a solution.
(Dissolution kya hai? Solution banne ke teen farzi qadmon ke naam likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Dissolution solute ko solvent mein hal karne ka amal hai. Qadam: (i) solvent ki intermolecular forces par qaboo (solvent ko phailana); (ii) solute ko alag alag hisson mein todna (solute ko phailana); (iii) solute aur solvent ka aapas mein mil kar solution banana.

book_ref.quote: It is assumed that the formation of a solution, takes place in three steps.

blocks.prompt:
46 Define standard enthalpy of solution. Give one exothermic example.
(Standard enthalpy of solution ki definition likhein. Aik exothermic misaal dein.)
blocks.explanation: Yeh woh heat hai jo aik mole substance solvent mein hal ho kar infinitely dilute solution banane par jazb ya kharij ho (ΔH°sol). Exothermic misaal: Na₂CO₃(s) + aq → 2Na⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq), ΔH°sol = –25 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The standard enthalpy of solution is the amount of heat absorbed or evolved

blocks.prompt:
47 What information does the magnitude of the heat of solution give?
(Heat of solution ki miqdaar kya maloomat deti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Heat of solution ki miqdaar un components ke darmiyan intermolecular kashish ki taaqat batati hai jo mil kar solution banate hain (maslan Table 6.2: NaCl 4.98, NH₄NO₃ 26.0 kJ mol⁻¹).

book_ref.quote: The magnitude of heat of solution gives information regarding the strength of intermolecular forces

blocks.prompt:
48 Name the two factors that govern the dissolution of an ionic compound.
(Ionic compound ke hal hone ko control karne wale do factors ke naam likhein.)
blocks.explanation: (i) Hydration energy, jo solute ions aur paani ke molecules ki kashish ko zahir karti hai. (ii) Lattice energy, jo mazboot electrostatic forces se jure ionic compound ke tootne ko control karti hai.

book_ref.quote: Hydration energy (accounts for the attraction of solute ions with water molecules)

blocks.prompt:
49 What is hydration? Name the forces involved.
(Hydration kya hai? Is mein shaamil forces ka naam batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Ionic compounds paani mein hal ho kar ions mein toot-te hain jinhein paani ke molecules gher lete hain. Paani ke molecules ka solute ions ko gher kar un se interact karna hydration hai. Paani ke molecules aur ions ke darmiyan forces ion-dipole forces hain.

book_ref.quote: When ionic compounds are dissolved in water, they are dissociated into ions

blocks.prompt:
50 What is enthalpy of hydration? Give its symbol and one value from the chapter.
(Enthalpy of hydration kya hai? Is ki alamat aur chapter se aik qeemat dein.)
blocks.explanation: Ions aur paani ke molecules ki ion-dipole forces ki kashish ki energy enthalpy of hydration (ΔHhyd) hai. Yeh kharij hoti hai (exothermic) kyun ke ion-dipole bond banta hai; maslan ΔH°hyd(Na⁺) = –406 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: The energy of attraction due to an ion-dipole force is known as enthalpy of hydration

blocks.prompt:
51 Define charge density of an ion. When is it large?
(Ion ki charge density ki definition likhein. Yeh kab zyada hoti hai?)
blocks.explanation: Charge density ion ke charge aur size ka mushtarka lafz hai (charge fi unit area). Chhote ion par zyada charge ho to charge density zyada; aise ions paani ke molecules ko zyada kheenchte hain, is liye un ki hydration energy zyada hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: We use a combined term for these two factors i.e., “charge density” defined as charge per unit area.

blocks.prompt:
52 Arrange Na⁺, Mg²⁺ and Al³⁺ in increasing order of enthalpy of hydration and give a reason.
(Na⁺, Mg²⁺ aur Al³⁺ ko enthalpy of hydration ki barhti tarteeb mein likhein aur wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Na⁺ < Mg²⁺ < Al³⁺. Na⁺ se Al³⁺ tak charge barhta aur size kam hota hai, is liye charge density barhti hai; paani ion ko zyada mazbooti se kheenchta hai aur zyada energy kharij hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: On the same basis we can explain the hydration energy of anions.

blocks.prompt:
53 Define lattice energy with an example.
(Lattice energy ki definition misaal ke saath likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Ionic crystal ki lattice energy (ΔHlatt) woh enthalpy change hai jab standard conditions par gaseous ions se aik mole ionic compound bane.
Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s), ΔH°latt = –787 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: “The lattice energy of an ionic crystal is the enthalpy change involved

blocks.prompt:
54 Why is the lattice energy of MgO (–3923 kJ mol⁻¹) much greater than that of LiF (–1049 kJ mol⁻¹)?
(MgO ki lattice energy (–3923 kJ mol⁻¹) LiF (–1049 kJ mol⁻¹) se kahin zyada kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: LiF aur MgO mein ions ki tarteeb aur size milte julte hain; asal farq charge ka hai. Doubly charged Mg²⁺ aur O²⁻ ki charge density zyada hai, is liye yeh singly charged Li⁺ aur F⁻ se zyada mazbooti se kheenchte hain aur mazboot ionic bonds bante hain.

book_ref.quote: These compounds have the same arrangement of ions in their lattice structure

blocks.prompt:
55 How does the size of the ions affect lattice energy? Give a reason.
(Ions ka size lattice energy par kaise asar dalta hai? Wajah dein.)
blocks.explanation: Cation ya anion ka size barhne se lattice energy kam hoti hai (Figure 6.6, alkali metal halides). Bade ions ki packing kam qareeb hoti hai, is liye mukhalif charge wale ions ki kashish kamzor hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Figure 6.6 show the values of lattice energies of alkali metal halides.

blocks.prompt:
56 Explain why the solubility of Group II hydroxides increases from Mg(OH)₂ to Ba(OH)₂.
(Wazahat karein ke Group II hydroxides ki solubility Mg(OH)₂ se Ba(OH)₂ tak kyun barhti hai.)
blocks.explanation: Group mein neeche hydration energy aur lattice energy dono kam hoti hain (cation ki charge density kam), magar lattice energy zyada tezi se kam hoti hai. Lattice energy haawi hai, ΔH°sol zyada exothermic hota hai aur solubility barhti hai.

book_ref.quote: For this reason, the lattice energy factor dominates this solubility trend.

blocks.prompt:
57 Explain why the solubility of Group II sulphates decreases from MgSO₄ to BaSO₄.
(Wazahat karein ke Group II sulphates ki solubility MgSO₄ se BaSO₄ tak kyun kam hoti hai.)
blocks.explanation: Sulphate ion (SO₄²⁻) OH⁻ se kahin bada hai, is liye MgSO₄ se BaSO₄ tak lattice energy thodi kam hoti hai, jab ke cation ki hydration energy zyada kam hoti hai. Hydration energy haawi hai, ΔH°sol zyada endothermic hota hai aur solubility kam hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Because the SO₄²⁺ is much larger than the OH⁻

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book correction: kitab mein SO₄²⁺ chhapa hai, sahi SO₄²⁻ hai. Aur jab ΔH°sol zyada endothermic ho to solubility KAM hoti hai, barhti nahi.

blocks.prompt:
58 Write the relation between lattice energy, enthalpy of solution and enthalpy of hydration from the enthalpy cycle of an ionic solid.
(Ionic solid ke enthalpy cycle se lattice energy, enthalpy of solution aur enthalpy of hydration ka taaluq likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Hess cycle (Figure 6.7) se: gaseous ions → solid (ΔH°latt), solid → aqueous ions (ΔH°sol), aur gaseous ions → aqueous ions (ΔH°hyd):
ΔH°latt + ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd, yani ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd – ΔH°latt.

book_ref.quote: We can calculate the enthalpy change of solution or the enthalpy change of hydration

blocks.prompt:
59 Calculate ΔH°sol of KBr: lattice energy –689 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(K⁺) = –322 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(Br⁻) = –347 kJ mol⁻¹.
(KBr ka ΔH°sol nikalein: lattice energy –689 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(K⁺) = –322 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH°hyd(Br⁻) = –347 kJ mol⁻¹.)
blocks.explanation: ΔH°sol = ΔH°hyd – ΔH°latt = (–322 – 347) – (–689) = –669 + 689 = +20 kJ mol⁻¹ (endothermic).

book_ref.quote: Step 1: Draw the enthalpy cycle

blocks.prompt:
60 Differentiate between lattice energy and enthalpy of hydration.
(Lattice energy aur enthalpy of hydration mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Lattice energy gaseous ions se solid banne ki hai; hydration energy ions ke gird paani ke molecules aane ki hai.

book_ref.quote: And as a result, all the ions in aqueous solution are said to be hydrated.

rows: Gaseous ions se aik mole ionic compound banne ka enthalpy change.
Ions ke gird paani ke molecules aane par kashish ki energy (ion-dipole forces).
Crystal mein mukhalif charge wale ions ki electrostatic forces ki wajah se.
Ions aur paani ke molecules ki ion-dipole forces ki wajah se.
Misaal: Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s), –787 kJ mol⁻¹.
Misaal: ΔH°hyd(Na⁺) = –406 kJ mol⁻¹.
Dissolution mein ionic compound ke tootne ko control karti hai.
Solute ions ki paani se kashish ko zahir karti hai.

blocks.prompt:
61 What is the Born-Haber cycle? Why is it needed?
(Born-Haber cycle kya hai? Is ki zaroorat kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Born-Haber cycle aik energy cycle hai, jo Hess's law ka itlaaq hai, aur kai tajurbati data se ionic compound ki lattice energy nikalne ke liye istemal hota hai. Is ki zaroorat is liye hai ke lattice energy aik seedhe tajurbe se maloom nahi ho sakti.

book_ref.quote: We can, however, calculate the value for ΔH°latt using several experimental data

blocks.prompt:
62 Write the steps that make up ΔHx in the Born-Haber cycle of NaCl.
(NaCl ke Born-Haber cycle mein ΔHx kin qadmon se banta hai, likhein.)
blocks.explanation: ΔHx = ΔH°at(Na) + ΔH°i1(Na) + ΔH°at(Cl) + ΔH°ea1(Cl): sodium ki atomization, sodium atoms ki first ionization, chlorine ki atomization (½Cl₂ → Cl) aur chlorine ki first electron affinity. NaCl ke liye ΔHx = 376 kJ mol⁻¹, aur ΔHx + ΔH°latt = ΔH°f.

book_ref.quote: Applying Hess’ law on the above energy cycle, we can write

blocks.prompt:
63 Calculate ΔH°f of LiF: ΔH°at(Li) = +159, ΔH°i1(Li) = +520, ΔH°at(F) = +79, ΔH°ea1(F) = –328 and ΔH°latt = –1049 kJ mol⁻¹.
(LiF ka ΔH°f nikalein: ΔH°at(Li) = +159, ΔH°i1(Li) = +520, ΔH°at(F) = +79, ΔH°ea1(F) = –328 aur ΔH°latt = –1049 kJ mol⁻¹.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔH°f = ΔH°latt + ΔH°at(Li) + ΔH°i1(Li) + ΔH°at(F) + ΔH°ea1(F)
= –1049 + 159 + 520 + 79 – 328 = –619 kJ mol⁻¹

book_ref.quote: ΔH°f = ΔH°latt + ΔH°at (Na) + ΔH°1i (Na) + ΔH°at (F₂) + ΔH°1ea (F)

blocks.prompt:
64 Define entropy. How is it related to disorder?
(Entropy ki definition likhein. Is ka disorder se kya taaluq hai?)
blocks.explanation: Entropy is baat ka paimana hai ke khaas temperature par system mein energy kitne tareeqon se bant sakti hai. Yeh randomness ya disorder (be-tarteebi) ka bhi paimana hai: zyada disorder, zyada entropy, aur system energy ke lihaaz se zyada mustahkam hota hai.

book_ref.quote: When the energy is distributed in more ways, a system is more stable.

blocks.prompt:
65 Six molecules of a gas are in jar A connected to an empty jar B. How many arrangements are possible after the stopcock is opened?
(Gas ke chhe molecules jar A mein hain jo khaali jar B se jura hai. Stopcock kholne ke baad kitni tarteebein mumkin hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Tarteebein = xʸ, x = jagahein = 2, y = particles = 6.
2⁶ = 64

book_ref.quote: Similarly, if there were 5 molecules initially in jar A

blocks.prompt:
66 How does the number of ways of arrangement explain diffusion?
(Tarteeb ke tareeqon ki tadaad diffusion ko kaise samjhati hai?)
blocks.explanation: Molecules ittefaq se phailte hain. Jab woh do jars mein phail sakte hain to mumkin tarteebein (2ʸ) bohat zyada ho jati hain, aur taqreeban sab mein molecules dono jars mein hote hain. Is liye diffusion hota hai kyun ke tarteeb ke bohat se tareeqe hain.

book_ref.quote: We can show that the molecules in a vapour diffuse by chance

blocks.prompt:
67 On what bases can the entropies of different substances be compared?
(Mukhtalif substances ki entropy ka muqabla kin buniyadon par hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: (i) Particles ki tadaad: kam particles, kam entropy (CaCO₃ 92.9 > CaO 39.7 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹). (ii) Sakhti: sakht substances ki kam entropy (diamond < graphite). (iii) State: solid < liquid < gas.

book_ref.quote: Entropies of different substances can be compared based on the number of particles, physical properties, and state.

blocks.prompt:
68 Why does diamond have lower entropy than graphite?
(Diamond ki entropy graphite se kam kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation: Milti julti chemical fitrat wale substances mein entropy sakhti se tay hoti hai. Diamond bohat sakht hai; is ki mazboot forces vibrations ko mehdood karti hain, jis se disorder ka imkaan kam hota hai, is liye entropy kam hai.

book_ref.quote: Stronger forces result in limited vibrations in harder substances which decrease the probability of disorder.

blocks.prompt:
69 What happens to entropy when sugar dissolves in tea?
(Chai mein cheeni hal hone par entropy ka kya hota hai?)
blocks.explanation: Chai mein cheeni hal hone se solute (cheeni) aur solvent dono ki entropy barhti hai, kyun ke particles mil jate hain aur bohat zyada tareeqon se tarteeb pa sakte hain.

book_ref.quote: Dissolution of sugar in tea increases the entropy of both the solute and solvent

blocks.prompt:
70 Using the chapter's values, find the entropy change when one mole of liquid water changes to water vapour, and explain its sign.
(Chapter ki qeematon se aik mole paani ke bhaap banne par entropy change nikalein aur sign ki wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: ΔS = S(bhaap) – S(liquid) = 188.7 – 69.9 = +118.8 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Yeh positive hai kyun ke gas ke molecules ki tarteeb ke tareeqe liquid se kahin zyada hain.

book_ref.quote: for water, it is 69.9 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹; whereas water vapour just above the boiling point is 188.7 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹

blocks.prompt:
71 State the rules used to predict an increase in entropy in a reaction.
(Reaction mein entropy barhne ka andaza lagane ke usool bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Entropy change positive hota hai jab (i) products mein solid liquid ya gas ban jaye, (ii) products ke moles zyada hon, aur (iii) gas molecules barh jayein, kyun ke gases ki entropy zyada hoti hai. Misaal: 2N₂O₅(g) → 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g).

book_ref.quote: If no. of moles in the products are more the entropy change is positive.

blocks.prompt:
72 Why is entropy change alone not enough to decide the spontaneity of a reaction?
(Sirf entropy change reaction ki spontaneity tay karne ke liye kaafi kyun nahi?)
blocks.explanation: Kuch reactions mein system ka entropy change spontaneity nahi batata; maslan CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ ka ΔS° positive hai magar room temperature par spontaneous nahi, jab ke Ca + O₂ ΔS°system negative hone par bhi khud react karta hai. Is liye free energy ki zaroorat hai.

book_ref.quote: when the entropy changes it may have positive or negative value

blocks.prompt:
73 Calculate ΔS°system for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g) using S°(N₂) = 191.5, S°(H₂) = 130.6 and S°(NH₃) = 193 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, and comment on the sign.
(S°(N₂) = 191.5, S°(H₂) = 130.6 aur S°(NH₃) = 193 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ le kar N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g) ka ΔS°system nikalein aur sign par tabsara karein.)
blocks.explanation: ΔS° = 2(193) – [191.5 + 3(130.6)] = 386 – 583.3 = –197.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (≈ –197). Negative: 4 moles gas se 2 moles gas banti hai, is liye disorder kam hota hai.

book_ref.quote: Let us calculate the entropy change of the system for the reaction:

blocks.prompt:
74 What is Gibbs free energy? Write its relation with enthalpy and entropy.
(Gibbs free energy kya hai? Is ka enthalpy aur entropy se taaluq likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Gibbs free energy (G) system ki enthalpy ka woh hissa hai jo doosri energy mein badal sakta hai. Baqi hissa T × S system ko us ke temperature par rakhne ke liye zaroori hai. H = G + TS; constant temperature par ΔG = ΔH – TΔS.

book_ref.quote: The heat content, or enthalpy (H) of any system is a combination of the following:

blocks.prompt:
75 When would all the enthalpy of a system be available for conversion? Explain.
(System ki saari enthalpy tabdeeli ke liye kab dastyab hogi? Wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation: H = G + TS se ghair-dastyab hissa T × S hai. Sirf zero kelvin par TS = 0 hota hai, is liye H = G aur saari enthalpy dastyab hogi.

book_ref.quote: It follows from the equation that all of the enthalpy of a system would be available only if

blocks.prompt:
76 What do ΔG > 0 and ΔG = 0 tell about a process?
(ΔG > 0 aur ΔG = 0 kisi process ke baare mein kya batate hain?)
blocks.explanation: ΔG < 0: process spontaneously ho sakta hai. ΔG > 0: process khud nahi hota; ulta ho sakta hai. ΔG = 0: na process na ulta khud hota hai; system equilibrium mein hai.

book_ref.quote: The system is in a state of equilibrium

blocks.prompt:
77 Differentiate between enthalpy (H) and Gibbs free energy (G) of a system.
(System ki enthalpy (H) aur Gibbs free energy (G) mein farq bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation: H kul heat content hai; G us ka woh hissa hai jo tabdeeli ke liye azad hai; H = G + TS.

book_ref.quote: This can be expressed as,

rows: System ka kul heat content, us ki structure aur physical state ki wajah se.
Enthalpy ka woh hissa jo doosri energy mein badal sakta hai.
H = G + TS (is mein ghair-dastyab hissa TS shaamil hai).
G = H – TS (TS ke baghair).
ΔH sirf batata hai ke heat kharij hui ya jazb.
ΔG ka sign process ki spontaneity batata hai.

blocks.prompt:
78 A reaction has ΔH = +30 kJ and ΔS = +0.120 kJ K⁻¹. Is it spontaneous at 298 K? Show working.
(Aik reaction ka ΔH = +30 kJ aur ΔS = +0.120 kJ K⁻¹ hai. Kya yeh 298 K par spontaneous hai? Hal dikhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔG = ΔH – TΔS = 30 – 298(0.120) = 30 – 35.76 = –5.76 kJ ≈ –5.8 kJ.
ΔG negative hai, is liye reaction 298 K par spontaneous hai.

book_ref.quote: For a process occurring at constant temperature,

blocks.prompt:
79 For the Haber process ΔH° = –91.8 kJ and ΔS° = –0.197 kJ K⁻¹. Calculate ΔG° at 350 K and state whether it is spontaneous.
(Haber process ke liye ΔH° = –91.8 kJ aur ΔS° = –0.197 kJ K⁻¹ hai. 350 K par ΔG° nikalein aur batayein ke spontaneous hai ya nahi.)
blocks.explanation:
ΔG = ΔH – TΔS = –91.8 – 350(–0.197) = –91.8 + 68.95 = –22.85 ≈ –22.9 kJ.
Negative hai, is liye 350 K par spontaneous (ΔH aur ΔS ko same maan kar).

book_ref.quote: Result: Since ΔG° is a negative value, thus it is concluded that Haber’s process is spontaneous
